chunks: The Shaykh, may Allah Most High support him, informed me from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Abān, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ibn Udhaynah, from Zurārah, who said:

One of the two of them عليهما السلام was asked about a man who began with his hand before his face, and with his feet before his hands. He said: “He should begin with what Allah began with, and he should repeat what had been done.”

key_terms.اللَّهُ: Allah; the source of the prescribed order in the ruling
key_terms.بَدَأَ: began; refers to starting the acts of wudu (ablution) in a particular order
key_terms.بِرِجْلَيْهِ: with his feet; refers to attending to the feet before the hands
key_terms.بِيَدِهِ: with his hand; refers to washing the hand/arm before the face
key_terms.رَجُلٍ: a man; the case under discussion in the ruling
key_terms.سُئِلَ: was asked; indicates the legal question posed to the Imam عليه السلام
key_terms.وَجْهِهِ: his face; the first limb mentioned in the proper order here
key_terms.يُعِدْ: he should repeat; indicates repetition of what was done improperly

ai.seo_question: What should someone do if he performs wudu (ablution) in the wrong order?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning the order of wudu (ablution). If a person performs the limbs out of sequence, he must return to the divinely prescribed order and repeat what was done incorrectly in that sequence.
